title: C6 vault records and the C7 byte shapes
description: From the vault release (E4): what the core keeps for the split-key vault (credential-protection-model.md, cred below) and the byte shapes C7's operations carry. These are not continuity state, so they are not in continuity-state.schema.json. bbolt holds one JSON value per key in five buckets: vault_users (vault_user, key the user_id), devices (device_record, key the pair user_id and device_id), grants (grant, key the grant_id), org_credentials (org_credential, key the reference), and import_receipts (import-receipt.schema.json ImportReceipt, keyed by import ID). For a confirmed save, the core commits sealed credentials and the complete secret-free receipt in one bbolt transaction; for discard or no-secret imports it commits the receipt before publication. The core writes personal profile mappings after publication as specified by target-import. U5 defines the buckets and the core writes them (U6 through U2's handlers); every record is new and no existing record changes, so an E3 core opens a file that holds them and ignores them. A user_id is the principal's login name (common.schema.json#/$defs/username), the only user identifier the contract has (Storage §5 names accounts by username). Every byte value is written padded base64 (RFC 4648 §4) on the wire, in these records and in shape fixtures, except device_id (base64url, common.schema.json#/$defs/device_id); known-answer and chain vectors are written in hex (vault-vectors.schema.json). Every AES-256-GCM blob is IV ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag with a fresh 12-byte IV per encryption and the associated data x-associated-data fixes (cred §4.1). Nothing here holds a passphrase, master_hash, Part 1, storage_key or encryption_key: those never reach bbolt (cred §3, §12). Part 2 is in Redis only (x-redis). Free text a person reads (references, labels, device names) is bounded here and rendered as plain text by every surface.

x-redis.value: Part 2's 16 raw bytes (cred §3.2), for one trusted device of one user; device_id in the key is its base64url form.
x-redis.ttl: Set on registration and on each Part 2 regeneration, renewed on each successful trusted unlock, to the config.yaml knob vault.part2_ttl (DEFAULT 43). Nothing else renews it.
x-redis.writers: The core only (Contract §8). Written only for a device on the allowlist, after part1 ‖ part2 opened the user's credential set (device-trust step 2; vault-unlock steps 7). Deleted by a revocation (device-trust step 5) and by a vault wipe (vault-unlock step 10). Untrusted mode never writes it (cred §5.1). Every read sits behind the allowlist check, so a Part 2 left behind by a revocation while Redis was down is unreachable and expires by its TTL.
x-redis.regenerable: Part 2 is derived (cred §9): losing it forces a regeneration with the passphrase, never a loss. A core never flushes Redis to remove it.

x-associated-data.encoding: The associated data of every vault blob, and the device challenge's signed bytes, are one encoding: a sequence of fields, each written as its length in bytes, a 16-bit unsigned big-endian integer, then the field's bytes; the first field is a fixed ASCII label naming the blob's kind and version. A text field is its UTF-8 bytes; a byte field (device_id, challenge) is its raw bytes, never its base64 or hex text.
x-associated-data.credential_set: fields: "tsb.vault.set.v1", user_id. The personal credential set (vault_user.encrypted_credentials), sealed under the user's encryption_key. Vector: C7/chain-set-seal.
x-associated-data.part1: fields: "tsb.vault.part1.v1", user_id, device_id (32 raw bytes). The sealed Part 1 the browser keeps (cred §3.1), sealed under storage_key; never on the server. Vector: C7/chain-part1-seal.
x-associated-data.org_credential: fields: "tsb.vault.org.v1", reference, unlock_class (its enum value as text). An org credential's blob (org_credential.sealed), sealed under the broker key (broker_unlocked) or under the storing administrator's encryption_key (user_unlocked), so a blob cannot move to another reference or class. Vectors: C7/chain-org-seal-broker, C7/chain-org-seal-user.
x-associated-data.device_challenge: fields: "tsb.device.challenge.v1", challenge (32 raw bytes), user_id, device_id (32 raw bytes), login_handle, operation. The bytes a device signs (device-trust, the challenge), built by the core from its own record of the challenge only. Vector: C7/chain-challenge-signed-bytes.

b64_16.description: 16 bytes, padded base64: user_salt, salt2, part1, part2.

b64_32.description: 32 bytes, padded base64: the device challenge (and, outside any wire, master_hash, storage_key, encryption_key).

sealed.description: An AES-256-GCM blob, IV (12 bytes) ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag (16 bytes), padded base64; at least the 28 bytes of IV and tag, at most 256 KiB.

signature.description: An ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256 signature in IEEE P1363 form, r ‖ s, 64 bytes (the form WebCrypto produces), padded base64.

public_key.description: A device public key: an uncompressed P-256 point as SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER (91 bytes), padded base64. The fixed prefix is the DER of the id-ecPublicKey / prime256v1 algorithm identifier and the point's 0x04 tag, so a key of another curve or form does not match. The core also refuses a point that is not on the curve (422). Any valid P-256 key is accepted, one a browser made non-extractable or one made in software: the core cannot tell them apart (DEFAULT 58).

challenge_operation.description: The one operation a device challenge is issued for (device-trust, the challenge). A signature made for one never verifies for another: the operation is in the signed bytes.

login_handle.description: The core's name for one login session inside a device challenge's signed bytes: returned with every challenge, the same for every challenge of that login, never the cookie's value (the cookie is HttpOnly, so page script cannot sign it).

challenge_id.description: The core's name for one outstanding device challenge; it says nothing of the challenge's bytes.

index_entry.description: One entry of a user's plaintext index: the reference and the kind only, never a label, login name or secret (DEFAULT 42).

user_salt.description: 16 random bytes from a CSPRNG, the argon2id salt of master_hash (cred §4.2). Public.

salt2.description: 16 random bytes from a CSPRNG, the PBKDF2 salt of encryption_key (cred §4.2). Public.

set_format.description: The format of the sealed set's plaintext: 1 is credential_set below.

encrypted_credentials.description: The user's personal credential set, one blob (cred §3.3): credential_set, UTF-8 JSON, sealed under encryption_key with x-associated-data credential_set. Initialised as a set with no entry, so the GCM tag always exists to check a passphrase against (DEFAULT 2).

index.description: The plaintext index: one entry per entry of the sealed set, in any order, each reference once. Written in the same bbolt transaction as encrypted_credentials, so the two never disagree (DEFAULT 42). The core reads from it, without an unlock, whether a reference exists and whether its entry carries a secret.

vault_user.description: vault_users bucket, key user_id: one user's vault (cred §3.3, as N1 item 5 reads it: per user, in a bucket of its own, not inside the login's account record, DEFAULT 22). Two states (the oneOf): minted, the salts only, written by the mint (POST /vault/salt) and never expiring; sealed, the salts with the sealed set and its index, written by init (POST /vault/init), which only a minted record allows. Deleted whole, in either state, by a vault wipe.

credential_entry.description: One entry inside a sealed set (or the plaintext of an org blob, org_credential_secret). key: login_name and the unencrypted private key's text (an encrypted key is refused at storage, DEFAULT 11), at most 16384 characters. password: login_name and the password, 1 to 1024 characters. none: no secret; a login name is optional and unused. The login name is the one sent to the target, never the target file's options.user (DEFAULT 52).

credential_set.description: The plaintext of a personal credential set (set_format 1): UTF-8 JSON, each reference once. It exists only in core memory while one establishment, store or delete is processed (DEFAULT 33); never on disk, in a log or on a wire.

device_pubkey.description: The device's public key (cred §3.3). Deleted by a revocation, in the same bbolt write as revoked_at and the audit line: its presence is the allowlist.

device_fingerprint.description: cred §4.2's device_fingerprint: the device_id itself, as the corpus stores it. No control: device_id is not a secret.

last_used_at.description: Moved by every verified challenge of the device: register, bind, unlock, regeneration (DEFAULT 60). The inactivity bound (policy.yaml devices.inactive_after) is measured from it.

revoke_reason.description: Who revoked it: its own user, a vault administrator (a wipe included), or the inactivity sweep.

owner_id.description: Reserved for RBAC tenancy (Storage §9), as on the session record; "" until then.

device_record.description: devices bucket, key (user_id, device_id): one trusted device of one user (cred §3.3; M6 (a)). On the allowlist exactly while device_pubkey is present. A revoked record stays, marked, for the audit and the list; re-registering the same device_id writes it afresh.

user.description: The principal granted the credential: a user until roles exist (DEFAULT 9).

selectors.description: The targets, in Storage §9's filter vocabulary verbatim (Storage §10.1a).

credential_ref.description: An org credential's reference; grants reference org credentials only (DEFAULT 8).

grant.description: grants bucket, key grant_id: Layer 2b (Storage §10.1a), (user × selectors) → an org credential. Each create, scope change and revoke writes its cred.* line first (DEFAULT 49).

org_credential_secret.description: The plaintext of an org credential's blob: UTF-8 JSON. login_name and secret are present exactly when the record's kind is key or password, under the bounds credential_entry gives each kind.

kind.description: Plaintext, so the core knows without opening the blob whether it carries a secret (DEFAULTs 42, 53).

sealed.description: org_credential_secret sealed with x-associated-data org_credential: under the broker key for broker_unlocked, under stored_by's encryption_key for user_unlocked (cred §8.2; Q5 (a)).

org_credential.description: org_credentials bucket, key reference: one org-vault credential (cred §8.2). No field describes what the account may do on a target: privilege tiering is rejected (cred §8.2).

credential_ref.description: A reference in this user's own index (layer personal). The core reads this field only.

profile_entry.description: One entry of users/<name>/profiles.yaml (Storage §10.3). Open: the other §10.3 fields (alias, notes, options_override, frontend) are kept as written and not read at this release (Storage §10.5).

profiles.description: At most one entry per target.

profiles_file.description: The parsed document of ~/.tsb/users/<name>/profiles.yaml, Layer 2a (Q7 (a)): the principal's own mapping of a target to one of their own credentials. Written only by the core, through POST /profiles/batch, read-modify-write of the one file and a rename into place (Storage §10.6). A credential delete or a vault wipe clears every mapping to the references it removes (O30).
